data.title: Wireframe
data.tagline: A wireframe is the page skeleton drawn in gray blocks and placeholder lines—it fixes "what goes where" before any colors or fonts.
data.learningOutcome: You can tell the wireframe stage from visual design, and ask an AI for a structural draft before styling.
data.description: Sketch the page in gray blocks first: how tall the header is, what sits in the hero, where the button goes. With positions settled, colors and fonts can be adjusted without reworking the layout. The wireframe fixes positions; the visual design handles colors and fonts.

learning.assumes: You have seen a floor plan or sketched a rough page layout.
learning.outcome: You can tell the wireframe stage from visual design, and ask an AI for a structural draft before styling.

distinctions.label: PRD
distinctions.explanation: PRD states for whom and what; Wireframe only shows where each block sits on the page.

distinctions.label: Visual hierarchy
distinctions.explanation: Visual Hierarchy decides which block reads first; Wireframe is the gray skeleton you arrange before styling.

explanation.title: Positions and sizes
explanation.text: Header height, hero footprint, card arrangement—structure questions get settled here, and changes only move boxes.

explanation.title: Placeholder text
explanation.text: Until real copy exists, label blocks as "one headline" or "one paragraph" instead of inventing content for the skeleton.

data.boundary: A wireframe is not a visual mockup: no colors, fonts, or images, so don't judge it by looks. It is also not a requirements doc—requirements say "for whom and what," the wireframe says "where." With an AI, split the rounds: confirm structure on the wireframe, then ask for visuals.

lessonPractice.title: The AI asks "what should the homepage look like?" and you only want to settle block positions. Which reply fits?

options.label: Draw a gray skeleton first: header, hero, cards, footer in position; colors later
options.feedback: Correct. The wireframe stage fixes structure only; visuals come after positions are confirmed, with the least to redo.

options.label: Build a finished version with gradients and fonts, and we'll react to it
options.feedback: With visuals already applied, moving one block drags colors, spacing, and fonts along—costliest time to restructure.

options.label: Just write all the copy; arrange the page however you like
options.feedback: Content does come first, but block positions need your confirmation too—"however you like" invites big drift.

data.agentPrompt: Start with a wireframe of the homepage: gray placeholder blocks marking header, hero, three cards, and footer with rough heights. Once I confirm the positions, apply colors and fonts.
